text:
kevin: Heads up — I'm opening a small TF change to the spot GPU pools to try instance-selection weighting, explicit per-AZ capacity constraints, and an AMI rotation hook. Goal is cut cost by ~12% while keeping pgp latency stable. PR coming in ~30m.

anya: Nice. Can you summarize the behavioral changes?

kevin: Sure — high level: 1) LaunchTemplate -> mixed_instances_policy with explicit weights for preferred GPUs (g6/g5 > g4dn) so we prefer cheaper newer generational GPUs but still accept older ones under pressure. 2) Add per-az target_capacity and fallback_capacity settings in the auto-scaling group to avoid unlucky single-AZ exhaustion. 3) Rotate AMI via SSM parameter and add lifecycle hook + small lambda to drain pods on replacement. 4) Add tags: "spot-tier" = "preferred|fallback", plus owner and rollout-phase for easier tracking.

sam: Are you switching instance types programmatically via weights or hard lists? any change to `mixed_az` logic?

kevin: We're using weighted_capacity in the `mixed_instances_policy` so TF will keep a single ASG but pass a list of instance type overrides with `weighted_capacity`. This means ASG can scale across types without new ASGs per family. AZ logic unchanged but we add `per_az_capacity` guardrails so we don't starve an AZ.

marta: Concern: ENI/IP limits for some instance types (g4dn.xlarge) might break pod density assumptions. Have we added admission/cluster limits?

kevin: Good call — adding instance_type to our nodeSelectorFallback script and a check in the TF plan about maximum pods based on ENI table. Will annotate the nodegroup with `eks.amazonaws.com/max-pods` on creation.

kevin: Example snippet I'm pushing in the PR (condensed):

```
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_spot_lt" {
  name_prefix   = "gpu-spot-lt-"
  image_id      = data.aws_ami.gpu_ami.id
  instance_type = ""
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }

  credit_specification { cpu_credits = "standard" }
}

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_spot_asg" {
  mixed_instances_policy {
    instances_distribution {
      on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 5
      spot_allocation_strategy = "capacity-optimized"
    }
    launch_template {
      launch_template_specification { launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu_spot_lt.id }
      overrides = [
        { instance_type = "g6g.4xlarge", weighted_capacity = "4" },
        { instance_type = "g5.2xlarge", weighted_capacity = "2" },
        { instance_type = "g4dn.xlarge", weighted_capacity = "1" },
      ]
    }
  }
  tag {
    key                 = "spot-tier"
    value               = "preferred"
    propagate_at_launch = true
  }
}
```

kevin: Also adding SSM param rotation and a lifecycle hook lambda pseudo-config:

```
resource "aws_sfn_state_machine" "ami_rotate" { ... }
# lifecycle hook triggers lambda that: marks node drain, waits for cordon/drain, then completes lifecycle action
```

anya: How are we handling interruption notices? any change to the interruption handler?

kevin: Keep current node-termination-handler but add a small sidecar script for pods that need longer shutdown windows. Also the ASG will prefer types with higher spot stability via `capacity-optimized` + our weighting.

marta: Rollout plan? I want gradual canary across two dev clusters first.

kevin: Exactly — staged rollout: dev-canary -> dev-wide -> prod-canary -> prod-wide. TF will be gated behind a feature flag `enable_instance_weighting` default false. We'll flip on canary clusters manually after smoke tests.

sam: Any cost estimate or perf risk numbers?

kevin: Preliminary: expected spot price reduction ~8-14% across regions tested (us-west-2, us-east-1). Risk: transient increased scheduling latency when switching between instance types (measured +20-40ms p95 for GPU allocation in dev). Not user-visible for async workloads but flagged for interactive.

anya: Thanks — please include a quick runbook for debugging: how to force fallback (set tag to fallback?), how to roll back, and who to page on prod regressions.

kevin: Will do. I'll post the PR and include the runbook + canary checklist. tagging @marta for rollout ops signoff. :thumbsup: 

marta: :eyes: I will review once PR is up. Please ensure monitoring alerts for pod eviction and cluster scheduling latency are enabled during rollout.

sam: Also add a small metric for `instance_type_change_rate` so we can watch churn.

kevin: Good call. Adding it to the console dashboard. PR in ~25m.

marta: :warning: Also add a playbook step: if per-AZ capacity lower than expected, revert to on-demand base capacity = 10% and notify infra channel.

kevin: noted.
